transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-21 | Start: 10:30 AM UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Montague - Head ML), Evan Clarke (Montague - Product), Sofia Ramirez (Montague - SRE), Calvin Ho (Montague - Data Eng)

Summary: Quick weekly POC sync to review last night's guardrail misfire reports, go over prompt-set scoring drift, and agree an immediate regression and canary plan. Some discussion of dedicated short-run capacity to repro with quantized model variant.

[00:00:08] Lena Ortiz: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i know there's a couple of incidents in the past 36 hours so we want to be pragmatic here and figure out repro and next steps, Marcus is going to walk through the regression plan.
[00:00:22] Marcus Chen: yep, i'll start, um so quick context - we ran the nightly eval sweep on the full pilot prompt set, about 6k rows, and we saw a 0.9% increase in guardrail triggers on the production routing variant compared to last week, most of which are short-answer hallucination flags and some safety false positives.
[00:00:38] Priya Nair: can you clarify - is that on hosted vs dedicated, or a model change? we didn't push anything from our side other than the dataset augmentation.
[00:00:46] Marcus Chen: good question, Priya. the uptick appears correlated with a routing change we executed last Thursday — small percentage of requests got routed to the quantized 16-bit variant to save cost during low-traffic windows. so it's likely a delta between fp16 kernels vs the quantized path.
[00:01:03] Evan Clarke: wait, we saw a note in the ticket that latency improved but some customers got a vague refusal, is that the guardrail you're describing or a separate issue?
[00:01:12] Marcus Chen: the 'vague refusal' is probably the safety classifier or reranker kicking in differently. when models produce shorter or lower-confidence outputs the downstream safety heuristic sometimes overindexes and flags. so you see both latency improvement and increased false positives.
[00:01:27] Sofia Ramirez: ok so SRE question — is there a way to correlate the exact model binary + kernel id with the logs? our infra only has request IDs, timestamp, and model tag.
[00:01:38] Marcus Chen: we can, yes — Redwood's runtime adds a runtime_model_hash and kernel_id in the trace header for dedicated/private customers; on hosted it's in the debug payload. we should be able to stitch that to your request IDs if you export the window around the incidents.
[00:01:52] Priya Nair: we'll do that, we'll roll the 48-hour logs and highlight the 12 examples that triggered guardrails in production. also, i want to note that many of these are from three prompt templates we introduced last week for returns handling. might be prompt drift.
[00:02:06] Marcus Chen: perfect, so plan A - targeted regression: we isolate those 3 templates, run them against three variants: baseline fp16, quantized-16-bit, and a slightly lower-temp reranked variant. we instrument scoring deltas, token-level perplexity, and guardrail score thresholds.
[00:02:24] Evan Clarke: what's our acceptance criteria? i.e., if we see a +1% guardrail trigger on quantized but everything else is fine, do we accept that or roll back?
[00:02:33] Lena Ortiz: good product question — for pilot success we agreed earlier that false positive delta should be under 0.5 percentage points on high-volume templates. anything above that needs either a prompt surgery or model pinning to baseline. for this week i'd recommend a canary: run dedicated capacity for 48 hours with quantized routing but with tighter reranker thresholds.
[00:02:51] Marcus Chen: and operationally we can set auto-fallback so if guardrail triggers exceed threshold we fall back to baseline model, so user impact is minimized. the runtime supports that.
[00:03:02] Calvin Ho: auto-fallback sounds nice, but can we avoid the cost of double inference? if fallback triggers we might double run tokens and cost spikes.
[00:03:12] Marcus Chen: correct — fallback adds cost. we can implement async verification: accept the lower-cost answer, run an async verifier on the background and if flagged then retract or mark. depends on product tolerance.
[00:03:24] Priya Nair: for returns handling we need synchronous accuracy — can't have retractions. i'd prefer model pinning until we fix prompt templates.
[00:03:32] Lena Ortiz: noted. action wise — Marcus will run a focused regression and include both sync fallback and async approaches in the report so you can choose.

[00:03:45] --- Topics: prompt surgery, scoring thresholds, regression test plan, canary capacity ---

[00:04:10] Marcus Chen: quick aside on scoring: we're seeing guardrail score thresholds were tuned on the baseline evaluation — the quantized variant's token distribution changes a bit and that shifts the reranker's calibration. small shift in logits cascades into higher safety scores.
[00:04:25] Priya Nair: is that something that can be re-calibrated post-quantization or does it require re-training the safety model?
[00:04:31] Marcus Chen: usually re-calibration (temperature correction, small threshold shifts) is enough for these deltas. full retraining only when distributional shift is large. we'll quantify in the regression CSV.
[00:04:43] Evan Clarke: any quick wins on prompts? Priya mentioned 3 templates — can we do whitespace or anchor tokens to reduce ambiguous completions?
[00:04:51] Marcus Chen: yeah, anchor tokens + stricter instruction formatting helps. also prefix-KV caching might be causing some stale context bleed if prompts changed rapidly; recommend using immutable prompt ids or canonicalization.
[00:05:05] Sofia Ramirez: regarding KV cache — we had one case where a customer-side change to prompt formatting didn't invalidate the cache and old context got reused, created weird partial answers. is Redwood's automatic prefix invalidation in pilot turned on?
[00:05:17] Marcus Chen: by default we do prefix invalidation for prompt-hashes on hosted. for dedicated/private there is a config toggle; I think for your pilot it's on but we should confirm. Marcus to check.
[00:05:28] Calvin Ho: i'll check our end too. i suspect the cache TTL configuration is 5 minutes which might be too long for returns where templates change often.

[00:05:40] --- Noise / minor crosstalk as someone juggles a doorbell ---

[00:05:55] Priya Nair: another incident note — one of the flagged examples was actually correct but matched a phrase in our deny-list; is there a way to reconcile user-intent context better?
[00:06:04] Marcus Chen: yes, the deny-list is a blunt instrument. switching to a contextualized allow/deny model (lightweight semantic embedding check before hard-block) reduces false positives. can add a reranking pre-check. that will add ~2-4ms overhead.
[00:06:18] Evan Clarke: that's fine if it reduces customer friction. what's the overhead vs the latency SLO?
[00:06:23] Marcus Chen: depends on batch size and routing. in dedicated we can reserve microsecond-optimized kernels; expected p95 increase of 5–8ms on the worst path.
[00:06:31] Lena Ortiz: tradeoff reminder — you asked earlier about dedicated short-run canary: the cost delta for 48 hours we estimated in the pilot doc, i'll re-share with updated numbers if we add an embedding pre-check.

[00:06:45] Sofia Ramirez: also we need to touch on compliance — if we start adding async verifiers or additional caching keys, does that affect data residency or KMS usage?
[00:06:53] Marcus Chen: not for hosted; for Private/VPC we integrate with your KMS and logs remain inside your account. any change to traces or extra debug payloads remain gated by your retention policy. we'll include that in the canary SOP.
[00:07:07] Priya Nair: we do want to avoid logs with PII in debug dumps; please ensure masking.
[00:07:12] Marcus Chen: absolutely, redwood has masking and we can provide filtered exports.

[00:07:25] Lena Ortiz: ok let's recap next steps before we run long: 1) Marcus regression across 3 templates + model variants 2) Montague to dump 48hr logs with request ids and flagged examples 3) SRE will enable trace level and confirm prefix invalidation config 4) Lena sends canary pricing and SOP.
[00:07:43] Evan Clarke: and decision gate — if false positive delta > 0.5pp on critical templates we pin to baseline; if <= 0.5pp we proceed with canary and prompt surgery on the bad templates.
[00:07:53] Lena Ortiz: yep that's our acceptance criteria. we'll also put an automatic fallback threshold in the canary so we don't impact live customers.

[00:08:05] --- End of formal agenda, quick parking-lot items follow ---
[00:08:15] Priya Nair: parking lot - we should evaluate the embedding-based allowlist; Marcus can you add a cost estimate?
[00:08:21] Marcus Chen: will include in regression doc, cost estimate + latency hit.
[00:08:26] Calvin Ho: and i want a quick note about the model hash in logs - please confirm format so we can hook to our observability.
[00:08:32] Marcus Chen: format is model:<model_name>-<version>-<hash> and kernel:<kernel_id>. i'll put exact schema in the notes.

[00:08:40] Lena Ortiz: great - thanks everybody. we'll reconvene next Thursday same time unless urgent. meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: Marcus uploaded a preliminary regression plan in the shared drive (link: https://app.redwood.dev/pilot-regressions/mtg-20270421), Lena sent a short note on a potential 48-hour dedicated canary pricing and will follow up with a formal SOP.

Transcription notes: speaker tags sometimes merged (Speaker 6 used for a short comment); minor mis-hearings around some kernel ids and proprietary naming.
